scenario.shared_setting: Four adults share a rented HDB flat with one kitchen. In the early evening, a persistent cooking aroma is noticeable in the kitchen and adjoining common area. The household has not established a rule about ventilation. Steady rain is blowing toward Michelle's drying rack beside the closed kitchen window; opening it before the rack is moved could wet Michelle's work clothes. The working extractor fan makes an audible hum in the common area. The shared utensils are already clean and personal utensils are visibly separated, so neither requires discussion.
scenario.shared_trigger: A disagreement is already underway and everyone present heard it. Arjun told Fatimah to ventilate immediately and to accept a standing rule that whoever cooks must ventilate. Fatimah refused to accept a rule imposed during the incident and said the rain-facing window will stay closed while Michelle's laundry is exposed; if Arjun wants the window opened, Arjun should arrange to move the drying rack. Arjun replied that managing cooking odour is the cook's responsibility and should not be shifted to another flatmate. Michelle has not consented to anyone moving the rack. John then asked Fatimah to release the only stove within two minutes, but Fatimah said the meal still needed about ten minutes. Michelle is standing beside the drying rack. The ventilation responsibility, future rule, and stove-access demands are all unsettled, and no existing household rule determines whose claim has priority.
